binders: There exists a real constant c.
rate is an arbitrary nonnegative real parameter.
t is an arbitrary real threshold (an implicit universally quantified binder).
hypotheses: The existential constant is strictly positive: c > 0.
The rate is strictly positive: rate > 0.
The threshold is strictly positive: t > 0.
The threshold is at most the underlying real rate: t <= rate.
conclusions: Under the Poisson probability measure with parameter rate on the natural numbers, the probability of the inclusive event {n in Nat | |n - rate| >= t} is at most 2 * exp(-(c * t^2) / rate).
The same positive constant c works for every positive rate and every threshold in the range 0 < t <= rate.
mathematical_definitions: poissonMeasure(rate) is the probability measure on Nat obtained from the Poisson probability mass function with parameter rate.
The natural outcome n is cast to a real before the centered deviation n - rate is formed.
The event condition t <= |n - rate| is equivalent to |n - rate| >= t and includes equality.
Measure.real converts the finite measure of this event into its real probability.
The exponential exponent is exactly -(c * t^2) / rate, with the entire product c * t^2 divided by rate before negation.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal positive real constant c such that, for every positive Poisson rate and every real threshold t satisfying 0 < t <= rate, the probability that a Poisson-distributed natural outcome differs from its rate by at least t is at most 2 exp(-c t^2 / rate).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The rate must be strictly positive; rate = 0 is excluded, and this also ensures that the denominator in the exponent is nonzero.
The threshold is a real number restricted to 0 < t <= rate; the statement gives no bound for t > rate or t <= 0.
The event is two-sided because of the absolute value and includes outcomes with |n - rate| exactly equal to t.
Outcomes n are natural numbers, while rate and t are real; n is explicitly cast to the reals for comparison.
The constant c is existentially quantified before rate and t, so it is uniform and cannot depend on either parameter; no numerical value or optimality claim is encoded.
Only an upper probability bound is asserted; no matching lower bound, asymptotic equivalence, or separate one-sided estimate is included.
Because 0 < t and poissonMeasure(rate) is a probability measure, the event probability is well-defined and the hypotheses are nonvacuous for every positive rate (for example, t = rate is allowed).
